subject: Forum selection & interim measures — AtlanticPay MSA questions
messages:
From: Samantha Greene <samantha@atlanticpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlanticPay Legal <legal@atlanticpay.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Forum selection & interim measures — AtlanticPay MSA questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the latest MSA + order form draft. Our counsel scanned the document and flagged a couple of items around dispute resolution that they want to clarify before we proceed to commercial redlines:

- Governing law: you currently propose California. We typically push for New York. Can you confirm Redwood's rationale for CA?
- Arbitration vs court: your draft is silent on arbitration. We prefer arbitration for final disputes.
- Interim injunctive relief: our legal team wants to ensure either party can seek emergency relief in a court of competent jurisdiction. They asked whether Redwood will accept a carveout for equitable relief in NY courts.

I've attached the redline our outside counsel started (AtlanticPay_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) and a short matrix showing the injunctive relief asks. Can we set a quick call tomorrow so we can align positions?

Best,
Samantha Greene
General Counsel, AtlanticPay
Attachments: AtlanticPay_MSA_Redline_v3.docx, injunctive-relief-matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@atlanticpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forum selection & interim measures — AtlanticPay MSA questions

Samantha — thanks for the note and the redline. Quick responses below, then proposed compromise options.

1) Governing law: Redwood prefers California (California law, state or federal courts in San Francisco) because of predictability for our commercial contract interpretation and our team/supporting counsel base. That said, we can be flexible if we get reciprocal protections on emergency relief.

2) Arbitration: Redwood is open to final disputes going to arbitration (non-aggregated, JAMS or AAA), provided the MSA includes an express carveout allowing either party to seek provisional/interim injunctive relief from a court prior to or during arbitration. We also need an expedited discovery path for injunction motion.

3) Interim injunctive relief / venue: Our suggested compromise is:
- Keep arbitration as the default for final disputes.
- Include express language that either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in the courts of either party's principal place of business (i.e., Redwood: San Francisco, AtlanticPay: New York) to avoid fights about forum for emergency measures.
- If AtlanticPay insists on NY-only carveout, we can accept that only if AtlanticPay agrees to reciprocal recognition (i.e., Redwood can seek interim relief in CA AND AtlanticPay can seek in NY).

Operational asks: if we agree to an NY carveout for emergency relief, we need an explicit SLO for Redwood to stop serving data for a court order that only applies to AtlanticPay (we'll loop in security/compliance).

Next steps: Laura and Marissa are on cc — Laura, can you take a quick look at the wording below and confirm we can propose to AtlanticPay legal? I can schedule a 30-min call with Samantha tomorrow afternoon.

Proposed sentence for the MSA (draft):
"Notwithstanding the Parties' agreement to submit disputes to binding arbitration, either Party may seek provisional, temporary or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction for the protection of its intellectual property rights or to prevent irreparable harm; such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the Parties' obligation to arbitrate other disputes."

I'll also attach a short injunctive-relief matrix showing tradeoffs.

– Karthik
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: injunctive-relief-matrix.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AtlanticPay MSA — forum + emergency relief posture

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal note on negotiation posture. High level: we should be cooperative but avoid conceding exclusive NY-only forum for injunctions without reciprocity and some limits. Suggested negotiation points: 

- Accept arbitration for final disputes (benefit: lower cost / confidentiality).
- Carveout for provisional relief: allow either party to seek interim injunctive relief in either party's home forum — this is clean and symmetric. If AtlanticPay insists on NY-only, push back and ask for: (i) reciprocal recognition; (ii) fast-track injunctive mechanism; (iii) costs-shifting if a party brings a frivolous emergency motion.
- Consider adding a notice / meet-and-confer obligation before emergency relief where feasible, but preserve immediate court access language for true emergencies.
- For Sales: if we accept NY-only carveout, ask for commercial concessions (e.g., 3% additional credit or shorter SLA cure window) — flag for finance.

Redlines to prepare: I'll mark the arbitration clause to include: arbitration (AAA/JAMS), seat mutually agreed, carveout language for provisional relief, and a short paragraph recognizing choice-of-law (California) — but we can entertain NY if AtlanticPay pushes hard.

I'll prepare a marked draft in an hour.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@atlanticpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forum selection & interim measures — AtlanticPay MSA questions

Samantha — thanks for the redline and the patience. We've reviewed internally (cc: Laura and Marissa) and propose the following consolidated approach:

1) Governing law: Redwood prefers California law (California substantive law) but will accept New York law if AtlanticPay confirms the interim relief carveout below and we agree a reciprocal recognition clause.

2) Arbitration + carveout (proposed language):
"The Parties agree that except for provisional, temporary or injunctive relief, all disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS (or AAA) under its rules. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek provisional, temporary or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, including courts in the State of California or the State of New York, and the Parties agree that such actions shall not be deemed a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate."

3) Logistics: we attached a short "injunctive-relief-matrix.xlsx" that explains operational impacts (who coordinates legal hold, notice windows, emergency contacts). We also request AtlanticPay confirm whether their counsel will agree to JAMS or prefer AAA — either is acceptable but we prefer JAMS for scheduling.

Ask: Can we hop on a 30-minute call Monday 10–10:30am PT to finalize? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and share a marked MSA (attached) capturing the language above.

Thanks — Karthik
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: AtlanticPay_MSA_Redline_v3.docx, injunctive-relief-matrix.xlsx
